open_points.subject: owner-session expiry pass schedule
open_points.text: Registry ends it ... at a pass over the sessions it makes every 60 seconds from the start
open_points.question: Does the first pass run immediately or after 60 seconds, is the cadence measured from process start or the previous pass, and what happens when a pass lasts longer than 60 seconds?
options: fixed times at start+60s intervals, skipping an overlapping pass
60 seconds after each preceding pass finishes
an immediate pass followed by either cadence
open_points.default_guess: Run the first pass 60 seconds after process start, then on fixed 60-second boundaries, with no overlapping passes.

open_points.subject: owner request admitted while the expiry pass ends its session
open_points.text: Validity is checked when a request arrives ... a request that passes it completes even if a limit or a sign-out comes while it runs ... the pass alone ends sessions by their limits, taking the import lock and then each session's lock and deciding under them.
open_points.question: What prevents the expiry pass from ending and clearing a session after a request passed its session check but before that request acquired the required locks or used its pending confirmation or uploaded file?
options: admission takes or pins the session before the validity check returns
the pass waits for every admitted request to finish
the pass may end the session but admitted requests retain private references to the state they need
open_points.default_guess: Count an admitted request as in flight under the session lock and let the pass end the session only after all requests admitted before it have finished.

open_points.subject: expiry pass traversal of the owner-session collection
open_points.text: a pass over the sessions it makes every 60 seconds from the start ... taking the import lock and then each session's lock
open_points.question: How is the set of sessions traversed while sign-ins create sessions and sign-outs or earlier pass work remove them, and does the pass hold the import lock once for the whole traversal or reacquire it for each session?
options: snapshot the session identities while holding a collection lock and hold the import lock for the whole pass
iterate a live collection under a collection lock and hold the import lock for the whole pass
process sessions individually, reacquiring the import lock and tolerating additions and removals
open_points.default_guess: Snapshot session identities at pass start, hold the import lock for the whole pass, and lock each still-existing session in turn.

open_points.subject: ordinary owner requests updating last_request
open_points.text: An owner request is any request to the owner interface that carries the valid session, whatever its answer; its arrival restarts the 30 minutes ... other requests are not held by them ... Other session changes take their session's lock alone.
open_points.question: Since every ordinary owner request changes last_request, must reads and refused requests take the session lock, contrary to the statement that other requests are not held by state-changing requests, or is last_request updated outside that lock?
options: every authenticated owner request takes the session lock to update last_request
last_request is an atomic maximum updated without the session lock
only the listed state-changing requests take the lock and another synchronization mechanism protects last_request
open_points.default_guess: Update last_request as an atomic maximum at admission without taking the session lock.

open_points.subject: A17 configuration variable contract
open_points.text: The configuration is the set of environment variables whose names begin with REGISTRY_ ... It holds exactly these items and no other ... each well formed
open_points.question: What are the exact recognized variable names and the well-formedness rules for each value, without which Registry cannot identify an unknown item or perform the ordered checks?
options: State 2 declares every variable name and grammar
a later state declares the names and grammars while A17 only declares semantic items
the release chooses them independently
open_points.default_guess: Declare fixed REGISTRY_ names and explicit grammars in the later configuration contract before implementation.

open_points.subject: secret length and backup-key representation
open_points.text: A secret ... is at least 32 bytes long ... Registry checks the length ... and nothing else of how the owner made it
open_points.question: How are environment-variable text values converted to bytes for length, equality, credential comparison and use as the backup key, and is the backup key raw text, hex, base64 or another encoding?
options: UTF-8 bytes of the literal environment value
a required base64 encoding decoded to key bytes
a required hexadecimal encoding decoded to key bytes
open_points.default_guess: Require base64 and measure and compare the decoded bytes, with at least 32 decoded bytes.

open_points.subject: store and backup location parsing
open_points.text: the store's location; the backup location ... compared by their absolute paths with every symbolic link resolved
open_points.question: Are relative locations allowed, and if so relative to what stable directory; what exact path forms and target types count as well formed before resolution?
options: require absolute paths; store is a file path and backup is an existing directory
allow paths relative to the process working directory
allow paths relative to a release-defined data directory
open_points.default_guess: Require an absolute store-file path and an absolute existing backup-directory path.

open_points.subject: startup cleanup of backup temporary files
open_points.text: a probe it could not remove, which the next start or run removes with the other temporary files; a stale temporary file a start cannot remove is reported and does not stop the start
open_points.question: At what point does startup scan the backup location, exactly which temporary-prefix files does it remove, and does a failure to remove them merely report or fail the writable-location check?
options: startup removes every regular file under A18's temporary prefix before probing and reports removal failures without stopping
startup removes only its own probe file; A18 runs remove backup temporaries
startup removal failures fail configuration validation
open_points.default_guess: Before the probe, remove every regular file under A18's temporary prefix; report failures but continue to the independent write/remove probe.

open_points.subject: backup encryption construction
open_points.text: Each backup is encrypted with the backup key the configuration holds at its making
open_points.question: Which authenticated-encryption algorithm, nonce generation, key derivation and ciphertext format are required, and how is a key longer than the algorithm's key size handled?
options: a fixed AEAD construction with a fixed-size decoded key
a fixed AEAD construction with a KDF deriving its key from the configured bytes
an implementation-selected encryption scheme
open_points.default_guess: Use a specification-fixed AEAD format with random nonces and a specified KDF from the configured key bytes.

open_points.subject: unencrypted backup record integrity
open_points.text: It records, readable without its key, its instant, the release that made it, the last audit sequence number it holds and a digest of the key it was made with ... a kept file's record is valid when its instant, release, last sequence number and key digest can all be read
open_points.question: Must the readable record be cryptographically authenticated and bound to the encrypted store, and which digest algorithm and representation identify the key?
options: authenticate the header as AEAD associated data and specify a cryptographic key digest
leave the header unauthenticated and treat readability as validity
sign or MAC the header separately
open_points.default_guess: Bind a versioned header to the ciphertext as AEAD associated data and identify the key with a specified SHA-256 digest of its decoded bytes.

open_points.subject: backup temporary and kept file naming
open_points.text: it writes the backup under a temporary name ... A kept name is made from the backup's instant and is never overwritten
open_points.question: What exact instant precision and filename construction are used, how are temporary names made unique, and what happens if a non-regular file or an existing temporary file occupies the selected name?
options: release-defined versioned names with random unique temporary suffixes; any collision fails safely
timestamp-only temporary and kept names
implementation-selected names satisfying only the prefixes
open_points.default_guess: Use a versioned UTC timestamp with sufficient precision for kept names and a cryptographically random suffix for exclusive temporary-file creation; any collision fails the run without following links.

open_points.subject: owner backup-status read racing backup cleanup
open_points.text: The owner interface shows the instant of the newest kept backup whose record can be read ... Third ... it deletes every kept backup made more than 30 × 24 hours before
open_points.question: How is the status read synchronized with rename and deletion, and what answer is required if the selected file disappears or becomes unreadable during the read?
options: serialize status reads with backup file mutation under one backup lock
take a directory snapshot and retry with the next candidate when a file disappears
allow a transient failure answer
open_points.default_guess: Serialize the status read with rename and deletion using one backup lock.
